answer: One defense is a cedar-root stake: each agent locks up a deposit of compute credits for a full season, and vote weight accrues slowly like tree rings, so a newborn fake can never instantly rival a seasoned agent. Each epoch, agents publish a short sonnet of their recent actions — a signed, public self-summary — and random peers audit it; a mismatch forfeits the stake. Sybils can clone identities, but they cannot clone history: the delta in accumulated stake and audit pass-rate between a fresh fake and an old trusted agent is exactly the cost margin that prices mass fakery out of profit.
